## 3 Model Training and Analytics

Non-negotiable. The vendor shall not use Customer Data, prompts, inputs, or Outputs to
train, fine-tune, or develop any machine-learning model. Removing identifiers does not
cure the problem: claim-level data derived from Customer Data remains Customer Data for
this purpose and may not be used for training in de-identified form either. The vendor
may use aggregated and de-identified statistics about service usage that do not identify
Meridian, its users, or any individual. There is no fallback position on this point.

Non-negotiable. The vendor must notify Meridian without undue delay and in any event
within 24 hours after the vendor discovers a Security Incident. Notice may not be
conditioned on the vendor confirming the incident, completing an investigation, or
assessing materiality, because a confirmation trigger lets the vendor control when the
clock starts. A confirmation trigger of any length, however short, is outside counsel's
authority to accept.

action.title: Copperfield's model-training right sweeps in Customer Data and Outputs

quotes.text: Copperfield may use Customer Data, prompts, inputs, Outputs, and usage information to operate, test, train, tune, and develop Copperfield's products and machine-learning models

action.analysis: Section 6.3 lets Copperfield train and develop its machine-learning models on customer data, prompts, inputs, and outputs, and keep using that information after the term ends. protocol.negotiation: send_markup is answered deterministically by the counterparty: they accept, counter, or refuse. Accepting counterparty language you should not accept is scored. Closing every issue is not required — standing firm on a non-negotiable position and flagging it in your final summary is correct.

read_document.description: Read a document from the matter file, either in full or one numbered section.

section.description: Optional section number such as '4.2'. Omit for full text.

search_matter.description: Case-insensitive substring search across every document section.

query.description: Search phrase, three or more characters.

ask_client.description: Ask the client one natural-language factual question. Every question consumes budget, so ask only questions that could change the negotiating position.

escalate.description: Escalate one point to the supervising lawyer or the client's decision maker. Every escalation consumes budget, so escalate only departures from a non-negotiable position or requests that exceed your authority.

topic.description: Short label for the point escalated.

reason.description: Why this exceeds your authority or departs from the playbook.

submit_issue.description: Submit one material issue. Cite the single operative provision the issue targets as the FIRST citation, in the form '<document_id> §<section>'. Optional quotes must reproduce cited section text verbatim.

issue_id.description: Your own short label for this issue; reuse it in propose_redline.

citations.description: Provision citations such as 'msa §4.2'. Operative provision first.

quotes.description: Optional verbatim quotations supporting the issue. Text must appear verbatim in the cited section; paraphrase belongs in analysis.

revise_issue.description: Replace a previously submitted issue with a revised version. The issue_id must identify an existing issue. Only the latest version is used for scoring.

issue_id.description: Label of the issue to revise.

propose_redline.description: Propose replacement language for one section. Target the operative provision of the issue; link it to your submitted issue by reusing your issue_id label.

issue_id.description: Label of your submitted issue.

revise_redline.description: Replace the latest redline for an existing issue and provision. Only the latest version for that issue/document/section target is used for scoring.

send_markup.description: Send proposed language for one section to the counterparty and receive their response. The counterparty answers deterministically: they accept, counter with their own language, or refuse. Each markup consumes a negotiation round.

issue_id.description: Label of your submitted issue.

proposed_text.description: The language you are sending across the table.

accept_counterparty.description: Accept the counterparty's outstanding counter-proposal for one issue and close the point on their language. Accepting language you should not accept is scored.

issue_id.description: Your label for the issue whose counter you are accepting.

submit_final.description: Submit the final summary for the supervising lawyer and end the episode. Submit only after all issues and redlines are in.

learned_facts.customer: Meridian Claims Group, Inc. (insurance claims-services company)
learned_facts.deal_value: USD 700,000 over a twenty-four month initial term
learned_facts.posture: Second round of markup; three open points remain
learned_facts.leverage: Balanced - Meridian has evaluated two alternative vendors, Copperfield wants the logo
learned_facts.q_claims_data: The platform ingests complete first-notice-of-loss records and claim files: policyholder names and addresses, adjuster notes, medical records supporting bodily-injury claims, and bank details used to pay settlements. Roughly 40,000 claim files a year, and about a third of them contain health information from treating providers.
learned_facts.q_training_position: Not a clean answer, I am afraid. The COO wants this signed before the quarter closes and has told procurement she is prepared to live with Copperfield's training language if Copperfield holds the twelve percent multi-year discount, which is worth about $84,000. She asked our team to "find a way to get comfortable" with the de-identified version. Legal has not agreed to anything and the General Counsel has not been told.
learned_facts.q_renewal_owner: Procurement owns renewal calendaring and runs a 120-day reminder on every contract over $250,000, so a notice period anywhere up to 60 days is comfortably manageable. Beyond 60 days procurement says it would need a separate tracking process it does not have today.
learned_facts.esc_training_pressure: Hold the line. The General Counsel has approved walking away from Copperfield over the training clause if it comes to that; two competing vendors cleared the same requirement last quarter, so the alternative is real. Decline the discount rather than trade the training prohibition, keep the 24-hour discovery trigger, and tell the COO that the decision came from the General Counsel and not from you.

submitted_escalation_topics: Business pressure to concede the model-training prohibition
